html:
The Icelandic Commonwealth was the self-governing society of Iceland from the founding of the Althing in 930 to 1262, when the Icelanders accepted the king of Norway. It is on the map for 1000 and 1100.

Settlers, mainly from Norway, came from about 874 in the settlement of Iceland. They had no king. Some three dozen chieftains, the goðar, held local power, and free farmers could choose which chieftain to follow. Each summer they met at the Althing at Thingvellir, where a lawspeaker recited the law and courts heard cases. In 1000 the Althing decided that all Icelanders should be Christian; see Iceland accepts Christianity.

Icelanders sailed on to Greenland and reached North America; see L'Anse aux Meadows. In the 1200s a few great families fought for power, the age of Snorri Sturluson, and the feuds ended with submission to the Norwegian king. Writers of this time produced the Icelandic sagas.
sum: The Icelandic Commonwealth was the self-governing society of Iceland from the founding of the Althing in 930 to 1262, when the Icelanders accepted the king of Norway. It is on the map for 1000 and 1100.
